lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | Aug 2022 - Jul 2024
- Owned the diagnostics service's monitoring dashboards across two major releases and the on-call rotation that used them.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases, adding automated regression checks that shortened release cycles from 2 weeks to 3 days.

- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue while rewriting the shared logging library, onboarding two new hires and taking over the weekend on-call rotation, which removed the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
- Raised diagnostic accuracy on 1,200 held-out cases from 71% to 79% by fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Cut p95 latency of single-request edge inference by 40% by serving the INT8 engine with dynamic batching.
- Using grouped tool-use rollouts, a composite reward over accuracy, citation validity and call count, and a GRPO loop with a frozen SFT reference, reduced end-to-end latency 5%.
- Stabilised GRPO training on sparse rewards by sampling a single rollout per prompt, so each update used exactly one scored trajectory.
- Documented the triage branch's abstention rules and escalation paths for the on-call reviewers, who adopted them as the team's runbook.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Cut p95 tool-call latency from 900 ms to 600 ms, a 50% reduction, by caching tool results and reusing completed sub-agent answers.
- Raised the runtime's task-completion rate by 12% on the benchmark suite, from 71% to 83%, by retrying failed sub-agent calls with their partial context.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Upstreamed 8 citation and faithfulness metrics to an open-source research-agent framework, where they now run in the default benchmark for every release.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Traced 3 structural pipeline defects in stability, sourcing and parameter handling to their modules with layered instrumentation; each was fixed upstream.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation, Kubernetes

items.says: The résumé does not identify one primary target identity.
items.because: The reader must infer whether the target is ML engineering, agent infrastructure, robotics software, or backend engineering.

items.says: The Mobility Systems internship is listed after the older robotics role and lacks visual priority.
items.because: The most recent completed and most target-relevant role should generally receive the strongest emphasis.

items.says: The concurrent M.S. and internship dates are not clearly presented as intentional.
items.because: A reader may briefly wonder whether the overlapping dates are incorrect.

items.says: The skills section omits several technical areas that are more strongly evidenced by the accomplishments.
items.because: Event-driven systems, CI/CD, inference optimization, quantization, caching, observability, and evaluation methodology are supported by the experience.

items.says: Some repeated locations could be removed if space is tight.
items.because: The space could be used for more relevant technical or academic evidence.

items.says: Punctuation and capitalization should be standardized across bullets.
The code link is ambiguous and does not indicate that it contains substantial technical work.
items.because: Recruiters may not investigate a generic-looking link deeply.

items.says: The M.S. entry does not explain what technical direction the degree supports.
items.because: Relevant coursework or research could strengthen an ML or AI target.

items.says: The expected-graduation detail should be retained only if it is relevant to the target roles.
The location is lower-value than relevant distinctions, coursework, research, or honors.
items.because: The degree title and institution are more important than the location.

items.says: The scope of “owned” is unclear.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether the dashboards were designed, implemented, maintained, or merely operated.

items.says: The bullet lacks a measurable operational outcome.
items.because: It does not show whether the work improved reliability, detection time, response time, or incident rates.

items.says: The phrase “the on-call rotation that used them” is conceptually awkward.
items.because: The dashboards serve the rotation, but the rotation using them is not itself an accomplishment.

items.says: The latency measurement context and test conditions are missing.
items.because: It is unclear whether the figures came from production, staging, or load tests and under what request volume.

items.says: The nature of the 200 ms threshold is unclear.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether it was a service-level objective or an engineering threshold.

items.says: The cache’s invalidation or freshness constraints are not explained.
items.because: Those constraints affect the credibility and tradeoffs of the intervention.

items.says: The scope of the latency improvement is unclear.
items.because: It may apply to one endpoint or to the diagnostics service broadly.

items.says: The direct contribution is obscured by the word “Maintained.”
items.because: The work should read as engineering enablement rather than ordinary CI maintenance.

items.says: The automated regression checks are not defined.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether they tested model quality, latency, data validation, compatibility, deployment, or integration.

items.says: The number of models or releases covered is missing.
items.because: The scope of the pipeline work is unclear.

items.says: The causal link between the automation and shorter release cycles is unclear.
items.because: The review asks whether the automation was primarily responsible for the change.

items.says: The operational effect of the checks is unspecified.
items.because: It is unclear whether they prevented regressions, reduced manual review, or both.

items.says: The bullet is overloaded with too many separate accomplishments.
items.because: It combines service migration, event-driven architecture, logging, onboarding, on-call ownership, and backlog elimination.

items.says: The bullet does not establish which action removed the nightly backlog.
items.because: The event queue, logging rewrite, and on-call work are combined into one causal claim.

items.because: If the backlog was only reduced, the résumé should state the precise level of improvement.

items.says: The onboarding and on-call details may distract from the architecture migration.
items.because: They should remain only when leadership or reliability ownership is important to the target role.

items.says: The rendered line wrapping around “on-call” should be checked.
items.because: The review identifies a broken “on-call” line.

items.says: The candidate’s ownership of the triage work is unclear.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether the work covered the model, feature extraction, service integration, or the full branch.

items.says: “Triage branch” is company-specific and undefined.
items.because: An external reader may not understand what it means operationally.

items.says: The pending-case backlog metric is not defined.
items.because: The reader needs to know exactly what was reduced.

items.says: The backlog result lacks a clear baseline and case volume.
items.because: It is unclear how many cases were processed or what comparison period produced the 68% figure.

items.says: The operational importance of the backlog reduction is not explained.
items.because: The bullet does not connect it to turnaround time, reviewer workload, or customer response.

items.says: “Diagnostic accuracy” is not defined for the task.
items.because: The experimental claim needs an auditable evaluation metric.

items.says: The base model or system being adapted is not identified.
items.because: The reader lacks context for the fine-tuning result.
